top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu) is the only awardable proposal on the slate, and I judge it on literary grounds rather than on the unanimous round-2 support. His voice is distinctive at the level of both the sentence and the whole book. Blinding and Solenoid, as publicly known, sustain a formal architecture at very large scale in which body, memory and dream are built into one cosmological imaginative project. That project reaches across prose and poetry and joins the intimate to the encyclopedic. The citation I support names the prose as the core and the poetry as its ground, and it avoids national or regional symbolism. Reservations remain: I cannot assess Romanian long-sentence rhythm and wordplay beyond translation, whether the later very long novels deepen the project or only extend it is unverified, and translation coverage of the poetry and essays is thin. The reading of the will's idealistic tendency is also an open interpretation. None of these is strong enough to prefer no award, so P000 is ranked last.
